title: Magna Carta (1215)
version: electronic text released 2021-05-17, most recently updated 2024-10-18 (the file's own header); the print edition is the first, Glasgow 1905 (title page and preface dated 6 February 1905)
converter: scratchpad scripts extract.py and build1215.py, not deposited (tools are kept outside commons; archived by the depositing session). extract.py finds the 63 headings 'CHAPTER ONE.' to 'CHAPTER SIXTY-THREE.' and the 'PREAMBLE.' heading in the section headed 'TEXT, TRANSLATION, AND COMMENTARY.', and takes, for each, the indented block that follows the Latin; build1215.py joins the wrapped lines of each block into one line, removes the 12 footnote markers (numbers in square brackets), drops the underscores that mark italics (the Latin legal terms in chapters 18 and 34), numbers the chapters 1 to 63 from the word headings (asserting that each word heading matches its position), and writes a four-line header then the preamble and the chapters. The Latin text, the commentary and the footnotes of the book are left out.
converter_checks: The script asserts that the 63 chapter headings are found in order and that each word heading names the number it is given. Each of the 64 blocks (preamble and 63 chapters) came out as exactly one paragraph. After the markers were removed, one square-bracketed phrase remains in the text, in the preamble ('[we have granted as underwritten]'), which is the book's own insertion. No character outside plain letters, digits and punctuation other than the curly quotes, the dash and the pound sign was found.
text_caveat: This is the translation as printed in a 1905 commentary, not the Latin charter and not a modern edition; the book does not say who made the English. The book's text of the Latin is, in its words, taken from the British Museum Trustees' edition founded on the Cottonian version No. 2 (footnote to the preamble). The division into a preamble and 63 chapters is a modern convenience, not the Charter's (the book says so).
